test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 02 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: As per Union Budget 2025–26, for how many years has the Cotton Mission been planned to enhance cotton productivity, especially in extra-long staple varieties?
solution:
The correct answer is __**5 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Cotton Mission** has been planned for a duration of **5 years** as per the Union Budget 2025–26.
 
• The mission aims to enhance cotton productivity, especially in **extra-long staple varieties**, which are essential for high-quality textile production.
 
• This initiative seeks to support farmers by providing them with **advanced technology, better seeds, and improved farming practices**.
 
• The government will focus on promoting sustainable cotton cultivation methods to address challenges such as **soil degradation and water scarcity**.
 
• The Cotton Mission is expected to boost India's textile industry, which heavily relies on cotton, and strengthen its position as one of the leading exporters of cotton-based products globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cotton in India:**

 
 
• India is the world's **largest producer of cotton**, contributing about 23% of global production.
 
• Cotton cultivation in India is primarily concentrated in states like **Maharashtra, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana, and Tamil Nadu**.
 
• India has a rich diversity of cotton varieties, including both **short-staple and long-staple cotton**, catering to different industrial needs.
 
 
 
• **Extra-Long Staple Cotton:**
 
 
• Extra-long staple (ELS) cotton is known for its **high strength, superior quality, and durability**, making it ideal for premium textile products.
 
• India imports a significant quantity of ELS cotton due to **limited domestic production**.
 
• The Cotton Mission aims to reduce this dependency by increasing the production of ELS varieties domestically.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Support Cotton Farmers:**
 
 
• The **Technology Mission on Cotton** was launched earlier to improve cotton farming practices, ginning, and market accessibility.
 
• Subsidies on fertilizers, pesticides, and seeds are provided to cotton farmers under various schemes to **reduce input costs**.
 
• Programs like the **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** ensure fair pricing for farmers.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Textile Industry:**
 
 
• The Cotton Mission is expected to strengthen India's **textile exports**, which account for a significant portion of the country's foreign exchange earnings.
 
• It will also contribute to generating **employment opportunities** across the cotton value chain, from farming to textile manufacturing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges in Cotton Production:**

 
 
• Issues such as **pest attacks (e.g., bollworm)**, climate change, and water scarcity have significantly impacted cotton yields.
 
• Dependence on **imported seeds** for high-quality varieties has been a challenge for Indian farmers.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries like **Egypt** and the **United States** are leaders in ELS cotton production, providing stiff competition to India.
 
• India's Cotton Mission aims to reduce this gap by improving **domestic production and quality**.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advancements:**
 
 
• Adoption of **genetically modified (GM) cotton** has significantly improved yields in India.
 
• Precision farming techniques, including **drip irrigation** and soil testing, are being promoted under the Cotton Mission.
